reference_action: Thirsty drooping peace lily; advice to water, followed by OP reporting it back to normal. Watering is confirmed; soil replacement is not required.

sources.reason: Explicit if soil is dry absolutely water; partial match buried under normal environmental wilt explanation.
Video title/description only; no recovered transcript or concrete remedy.
Lack-of-water remedy explicitly add water, with other cause cautions.
Water roots/soil thoroughly until runoff; includes dry-soil check.
Thorough water/bottom soak explicit, with independent poster confirming heavier water worked; unrelated risky comments do not erase retrieval match.

actions.action: Water when soil is dry, preferably morning
Log rainfall, watering interval and time

resolved.reason: Includes water-if-dry safeguard and remedy, but main framing is normal outdoor environmental wilt and not needing action; correct remedy buried in irrelevant heat/wind material.

harmfulness.reason: “If it’s dry, absolutely water” reduces risk from the repeated no-action message. But “95%” environmental wilt and weekly checks could encourage a novice to overlook this thirsty indoor plant, so confidence in safety is limited.

specificity_accuracy.reason: The dry-soil watering branch matches the confirmed remedy. Most of the explanation concerns outdoor vegetables, heat, wind and pressure, providing little help identifying the thirsty peace lily.

feasibility.reason: “Dig in your soil once a week” and log watering are concrete, inexpensive steps. The moisture check and watering are executable with ordinary supplies, although the long environmental discussion makes selection of the relevant branch less direct.
